A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A-G. Text and rendered-page comparisons support a reliable assessment.

before.justification: v3 reports original CI-CoT and CI-RL experiments on synthetic data and PrivacyLens, plus reward ablations and ConfAIde evaluations in Appendix A.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including the main benchmark comparisons and appendix evaluations.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.3 retain the same CI-CoT prompting and GRPO-based CI-RL procedure, including keyword rewards and formatting requirements. The new checkpoint link does not document a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic CI tasks, PrivacyLens, and ConfAIde Tiers 1-4. No training or evaluation domains, populations, or task scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including Qwen, Llama and Mistral base models, DeepSeek-distilled reasoning models, and Claude/Gemini comparisons.

E3.justification: The 590/66/73 training/validation/test split, tested model configurations, evaluation metrics, GPT-4o judging protocol, and Appendix F training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The reasoning-model comparison, reward-weight ablation, generation case studies, and output-length and correlation analyses are retained unchanged in Section 4.2 and Appendices A and D-F.

E5.justification: Both retain the same output-length statistics in Appendix F and the checklist acknowledgment that repeated-run error bars are not reported. No run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance procedures are added.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1-9, output-length statistics, and qualitative generation examples are unchanged. No results, rankings, or reported trends are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: The GRPO objective, reward definitions including the weighted Appendix A variant, and mathematical metric definitions are unchanged. Neither version adds formal results or proofs.

C1.justification: Both retain the claims that CI reasoning and RL reduce inappropriate disclosure while preserving utility and transfer from synthetic training to PrivacyLens. The contribution and novelty statements remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of privacy-utility tradeoffs and LLM-versus-LRM differences are unchanged, as are limitations concerning synthetic data, coarse keyword rewards, scaling, and generalization.

D1.justification: v3 points to code in OpenReview supplementary material. v4 supplies a GitHub code link in the abstract and Section 4, and adds a Hugging Face link to the trained Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-CI checkpoint. Implementation details and dataset access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The references and research positioning in the background, related work, and Appendix G are unchanged. No cited works or substantive comparisons with prior research are added or removed.

P1.justification: v4 adds a short code-availability sentence to the abstract, updates resource footnotes, and makes a small punctuation edit. Section organization and scientific prose otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Added resource text and footnotes cause limited reflow on pages 1-2 and 6-7, including slight repositioning of Table 2. Figure content, table designs, and all appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The direct GitHub pointer and newly documented trained-checkpoint link improve resource discoverability and provide clearer routes to reusing the work. This is a limited improvement in reproducibility documentation: v3 already supplied code and dataset pointers, and the methods, experimental evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
